title: Etale descent for finite constant-group torsors with equivariant maps
statement: Let $S$ be a scheme [def-pc-scheme], in the universes of [def-weil-size-convention], let $H$ be a finite abstract group, and let $V$ be an arbitrary $S$-scheme with a left $H$-action by $S$-automorphisms. For an $S$-scheme $T$, let $H_T=\coprod_{h\in H}T$ with multiplication induced by that of $H$. A left $H_T$-torsor is a $T$-scheme $P\to T$ with a left $H_T$-action which becomes equivariantly isomorphic to $H_{T_i}$ with left translation after some jointly surjective family of etale maps $T_i\to T$ [def-weil-etale-morphism]. Let $\mathcal T_V(T)$ have objects $(P,f)$ consisting of such a torsor and an $H$-equivariant $S$-morphism $f:P\to V$. Its arrows are $H_T$-equivariant $T$-isomorphisms $b:P\to P'$ satisfying $f' b=f$. Pullback along $T'\to T$ is by scheme fibre product [def-pc-fibre-product], with the induced action and map. Then $\mathcal T_V$ is a stack in groupoids for the etale topology: for any two objects over $T$, the presheaf of their isomorphisms on $S$-schemes over $T$ is a sheaf for jointly surjective etale families; and for every such family $\{T_i\to T\}$, any objects $(P_i,f_i)$ with overlap isomorphisms $b_{ij}$ satisfying $b_{jk}b_{ij}=b_{ik}$ on triple overlaps are restrictions of an object $(P,f)$ over $T$, via isomorphisms inducing the specified $b_{ij}$. Stack and groupoid have the conventions of [def-sfb-stable-pointed-moduli-groupoids]. No freeness of the action on $V$, finite-type hypothesis on $V$ or $S$, or invertibility of $|H|$ is required.

proof.text: Pullback preserves the torsor condition: pull a trivializing etale family back along $T'\to T$ and use the canonical fibre-product identifications. The pulled-back family is still jointly surjective etale. Pullback of the map to $V$ is its composite with the projection to $P$; it is equivariant. An equivariant isomorphism and its inverse pull back to equivariant isomorphisms respecting that map. The universal property of fibre products supplies the unit and associativity comparisons, whose coherence follows because both composites have the same projections. Thus these groupoids and pullbacks give a category fibred in groupoids in the convention stated in the item.

source.place: Tag 0370, construction preceding lemma-group-quotient-stack-in-groupoids; cartesian pullbacks

proof.text: For any jointly surjective etale family $\{T_i\to T\}$, apply the fpqc-covering lemma with ambient small etale site $T_{\mathrm{Et}}$ and object $\mathrm{id}_T$. It is therefore an fpqc family. Its pullback along any scheme map is again a jointly surjective etale family, hence fpqc by the same argument. In particular this applies to $P\times_TT_i\to P$ for every $T$-scheme $P$. Compatible maps from these schemes to any fixed scheme glue uniquely by representable fpqc descent. If the maps are over a base, their composite with that base equals the required structure map because this equality holds on the cover and gluing is unique.

Every torsor $P\to T$ occurring here is finite etale. Indeed take a trivializing family $U_a\to T$. For a finite set $H$ the fold $\coprod_H U_a\to U_a$ is etale by finite coproduct etaleness, applied to identity morphisms. It is finite: on an affine open $W=\operatorname{Spec}A\subset U_a$, its inverse image is $\coprod_H W=\operatorname{Spec}(\prod_H A)$, and the diagonal algebra $A\to\prod_H A$ is generated as an $A$-module by the finitely many coordinate vectors. This proves finiteness on an affine cover, hence globally. The trivializations identify these folds with the pullbacks of $P\to T$. Step 2 makes the trivializing family fpqc; descend finiteness and etaleness to $P\to T$.

source.place: Tag 0BLZ, lemma-finite-etale-stack; Descent Tags 02LA and 02VN applied to trivializations

proof.text: Fix two global objects $(P,f),(Q,g)$ and compatible isomorphisms between their restrictions to a jointly surjective etale family. View their underlying maps as maps $P\times_TT_i\to Q$, and glue them by Step 2 to $b:P\to Q$. Glue the local inverses likewise to $c:Q\to P$. The equations $cb=1$, $bc=1$ and $gb=f$ hold by uniqueness on the respective pulled-back covers. For every $h\in H$ the two maps $b\circ h_P$ and $h_Q\circ b$ agree on $P\times_TT_i$, hence are equal. Thus $b$ is equivariant and is an arrow of the required groupoid. Uniqueness of $b$ follows from the same gluing uniqueness. Apply this argument after any $T'\to T$ to obtain exactly the sheaf assertion on the entire category of $S$-schemes over $T$.

source.place: Tag 0370, omitted morphism-descent axiom, expanded using Descent Tag 023Q

proof.text: Now take object descent data $(P_i,f_i,b_{ij})$ on $\{T_i\to T\}$. By Step 3 each $P_i\to T_i$ is finite etale. Form $T^*=\coprod_iT_i$ and $P^*=\coprod_iP_i$; $P^*\to T^*$ is finite etale by Zariski locality on the open-and-closed summands. The morphism $T^*\to T$ is a surjective etale morphism (the coproduct of an etale covering, explicitly allowed in the finite-etale descent lemma). On $T^*\times_TT^*$ the summands are $T_i\times_TT_j$: this follows by restricting each projection to the disjoint open summands and applying the fibre-product universal property. Thus the $b_{ij}$ assemble to an isomorphism of the two pullbacks of $P^*$; the triple-overlap cocycle is precisely the given one on each summand. Apply finite etale descent to obtain a finite etale $P\to T$ and isomorphisms $e_i:P\times_TT_i\xrightarrow{\sim}P_i$ with $b_{ij}=e_j e_i^{-1}$ on overlaps.

source.place: Tag 0BLZ, lemma-finite-etale-stack; family encoded by its disjoint union, as in lem-galois-descent

proof.text: For each $h\in H$, transport the action of $h$ on $P_i$ across $e_i$ to an automorphism of $P\times_TT_i$. These maps are compatible on overlaps because $b_{ij}$ is equivariant. Step 2 glues them to $a_h:P\to P$ over $T$. The identities $a_1=1$ and $a_g a_h=a_{gh}$ follow by gluing uniqueness, since they hold on every $P_i$; in particular $a_{h^{-1}}$ is inverse to $a_h$. The coproduct mapping property makes the maps $a_h$ a morphism $H_T\times_TP=\coprod_H P\to P$, and those identities are exactly a left action. Under $e_i$ it is the original action. Choose trivializing etale families for each $P_i$. Their composites with $T_i\to T$ are a jointly surjective etale family and equivariantly trivialize $P$. Thus $P$ is a torsor in precisely the etale-local sense of the item.

source.place: Tag 0370, descent of torsor action; torsor local trivializations composed with original cover

proof.text: The morphisms $f_i e_i:P\times_TT_i\to V$ agree on overlaps, since $f_j b_{ij}=f_i$. Step 2 gives a unique map $f:P\to V$; it is over $S$ by equality on this cover. For each $h\in H$, $f a_h=h_V f$ holds after restriction to every $P_i$, so it holds globally by the same uniqueness. Consequently $(P,f)$ is an object and each $e_i$ is an equivariant isomorphism respecting maps to $V$. Their overlap maps are the prescribed $b_{ij}$ by Step 5. This proves effective object descent; together with Steps 1 and 4 it proves the claimed stack property. None of these arguments requires a free action on $V$, finite type, or a unit $|H|$.
